vra:descriptionSet.vra:display: Mudayrib is located about 130 km south-east of Muscat in the Wilāyat of Al Qābil in Ash Shariqīyah North Governorate on the northern edges of Ash Shariqīyah desert (formerly, Wahiba Sands; Ramlat Āl Wahībah). It is located on the eastern banks of the Wādī al Mudayrib, which runs in a south-easterly direction along the foothills of the Eastern Ḩajar mountains (Al-Ḥajar ash-Sharqī). Lying on the main inland route from the eastern port of Şūr to the interior of Oman, Mudayrib has always benefited from Indian Ocean trade. Unlike many other oases of the region Mudayrib consists of a single settlement core rather than having a fragmentary setup. The settlement itself is nestled within a ring of low ophiolite hills which surround the urban core on all sides except the southern one, where the oasis fan outwards. The water of the irrigation system, Falaj al Mudayrib, is tapped from the wadī about 6 km to the north of the settlement and branches into four main channels (sāqīyat) near the sūq are the actual irrigational component of the aflāj network. The surrounding hills are surmounted by guard towers which scan the surrounding countryside and main approaches to the settlement. The largest hill, sloping upwards on the eastern edge of the settlement holds at its summit the widely visible Ḩisn al Mudayrib, a fortified enclosure used in times of strife with no residential functions. The relatively compact and self-contained form of the settlement is partly explained by the topographical limitations which the surrounding hills posed on the expansion of the settlement and partly due to the strong position of the Ḩirth tribes in the Ibrā’ and Al Qābil regions. The core is disposed around a series of fortifications, such as the Ḩisn al Khanājīra, located at the centre of Mudayrib, immediately to the west of the sūq. The settlement quarter is an excellent example of the traditional architectural development that reached impressive refinement and high levels of quality.

vra:description.source: Bandyopadhyay, Soumyen et al, Documentation and Heritage Management and Development Plan: Al-Mudayrib, Al-Qabil, Nottingham: Nottingham Trent University, 2014

vra:descriptionSet.vra:display: Ethnographic video interview of local inhabitants talking about the past appearance of Mudayrib settlement, Oman. The inhabitants were interviewed by ArCHIAM. Following ArCHIAM's drawn and photographic documentation during the fieldwork a series of interviews were carried out with erstwhile inhabitants of the hārat. These interviews' ethnographic dimension aim to, by providing an expansive account of the oasis’ oral history, establish the tribal ownership pattern of dwellings within the hārah and thus provide a deeper insight into the morphological development of the urban layout.
